To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inhibition of CRPM2 phosphorylation at S522 in CRMP2-KI mice induces the suppression of somatic atrophy, dendritic spine reduction and axonal degeneration in sensorimotor cortices after spinal cord injury.

the inhibition of collapsin responsive mediator protein 2 phosphorylation at ser522 in the CRMP 2 knock in mice model, leads to the up regulation of genes involved in energy metabolism and neuronal pathway, which is associated with the improvement of the structural pathophysiological condition of the axotomized neuron and its neighboring neuron after spinal cord injury.
CRMP2 phosphorylated by GSK-3β at Ser522 inhibits the axon regeneration and the lost sensory motor function after spinal cord injuries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transcriptome analysis of the sensorimotor cortex of wild type mice and CRMP2KI knock in mice after spinal cord injury.
the molecular mechanism in axotmized neurons after spinal cord injury in CRMP2 knockout mice.
the transcriptome analysis of the sensorimotor cortex after spinal cord injury using micro dissection punch system and CRMP2 knockin mouse model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CRMP2 phosphorylated at Ser522 is a negative regulator of axon regeneration, and the inhibition of CRPM2 phosphorylation at the same site is a potential therapeutic strategy for SCI.
the transcriptome analysis after SCI revealed the regenerative mechanism and pathophysiology of central nervous system after SCI in CRMP2KIKI mice.
the CRMP2KI mouse model has shown to have improved structural and transcriptomic changes after spinal cord injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CRMP2 is an important molecule for axon regeneration and neuronal survival in the central nervous systems.

the CRMP2 phosphorylated at Ser522 is a negative regulator of axon regeneration after SCI and inhibition of CRMP phosphorylation at this site leads to the improvement of axotomized neuron survival, axon regeneration, and functional recovery.

the inhibition of phosphorylation of CRMP2 at Ser522 induces axon elonga-tion and partial recovery of lost sensorimotor functions after SCI, and the underlying mechanism of axotomized neuron regeneration in the central nervous systems may involve a whole-body metabolic system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CRMP2 is not only a key molecule in axonal elongation, but it is also involved in the regulation of the whole central nervous system after SCI.
CRMP2 phosphorylated at Ser522 plays an important role in the recovery of the lost function of the central nervous system after SCI.
the CRMP2KI mouse model is an effective SCI animal model to investigate the regenerative mechanism in the central nervous systems.
